    Koreans fought for their democracy

    Supporting explanation

    South Koreans fought for their democracy. Gwangju in 1980, the movement of 1987, and resistance to the martial-law declaration in December 2024 belong in that history. Citizens, journalists, legislators and institutions acted. The crisis did not end in one night, but Korean society had people prepared to defend its political rights.

    Those people have their own views about America, China, Japan, North Korea, and their government’s decisions. We should expect arguments. We should expect governments to change course. That is part of taking Korean democracy seriously.

    Sources and supporting detail

    Koreans fought for their democracy

    Evidence and earlier preparation · martial-law

    Evidence and preparation

    This belongs in our account of a global player. On December 3, 2024, President Yoon Suk Yeol declared martial law. Citizens resisted and lawmakers reached the Assembly, which voted 190–0 at 1:02 a.m. on December 4 to demand its end. Yoon announced withdrawal later that morning and the cabinet approved it. Parliament impeached him on December 14; the Constitutional Court removed him on April 4, 2025. These are different steps, not a crisis resolved in one night. Democratic resilience came from people acting and institutions doing their work. Removal did not end political conflict or guarantee future resilience. Americans can learn from Korea’s constitutional experience, too. The 34-second montage restores the original talk’s footage. No autoplay; pause when leaving this slide.

    1980: Gwangju street procession. SNU historical photograph collection, attributed there to the May 18 Memorial Foundation. Exact day and photographer not supplied.

    1987: Seoul, Gwanggyo demonstration; exact date unknown. Photograph by Jeon Min-jo, National Museum of Contemporary Korean History. Archive image and KOGL Type 1 attribution. Do not assign a specific June date to this image.

    2024: Reuters video still, published by The Guardian. Ahn Gwi-ryeong was a Democratic Party spokesperson, not a sitting lawmaker. Reuters interview, December 5, 2024, Jisoo Kim and Daewoung Kim. The confrontation took place during the December 3–4 martial-law night. No claim that she dared the soldier to shoot or that the weapon was loaded.

    The Assembly voted 190–0 to demand an end to martial law. On April 4, 2025, the Constitutional Court removed Yoon. Citizens. Parliament. Courts. This was not a crisis resolved in one night. The images show civic action; they do not imply that one person alone ended the crisis. The previous vote-count video is retained in the round 45 backup.

    Media use: local editorial presentation only. No open license established for the Gwangju or Reuters images; no public deployment authorized in this revision.

    Independent choices. An enduring alliance.

    Korean agency

    Defense responsibility
    Negotiated terms

    +

    American ties

    Security
    Technology and investment

    November 2025 · U.S.–ROK agreement

    Continued U.S. forces · work toward wartime operational-control transfer · investment funding terms

    Supporting explanation

    My expectation is that South Korea will neither do whatever Washington says nor break its American ties. Both expectations misunderstand the relationship.

    The November 2025 joint agreement reaffirmed the American defense commitment and the continued presence of U.S. forces. It also committed both sides to work toward transferring wartime operational control. South Korea seeks greater responsibility for its own defense within a continuing alliance.

    The same agreement put conditions on the timing of funding for its strategic investment arrangement, including an annual dollar-funding ceiling. Korea negotiated terms that addressed its own financial stability. Partnership includes bargaining.

    When the next disagreement makes the news, remember the connections behind it. Security, technology, investment, people and institutions give both countries reasons to remain engaged. Korean independence and a durable American relationship can develop together.

    North Korea is going to endure

    ControlInstitutions and repression
    DeterrenceNuclear weapons and missiles
    SupportChanging external relationships
    AdaptationState ownership and markets

    My expectation · next 10–15 years · state power and people’s welfare require different evidence

    Supporting explanation

    Now the North. I do not expect it to collapse. North Korea survived the loss of its Soviet partner, catastrophic famine, leadership transitions, sanctions, and the pandemic border closure. Waiting for the next crisis to finish it off has repeatedly failed to explain what happened.

    Start with powerful institutions of control. Repression prevents organized challenges; military and security priorities shape resources. State strength and the welfare of the people require different evidence.

    The night image shows a real difference in electricity and settlement when it was taken. It cannot tell us when a government will fall, how every household lives, or what has changed since then.

    Evidence and earlier preparation · russia

    Evidence and preparation

    The June 2024 treaty formalized a deeper partnership. North Korean arms and soldiers support Russia's war; the relationship provides Pyongyang with resources, diplomatic protection and military benefits. The May 2025 Multilateral Sanctions Monitoring Team report documents transfers and cooperation. It is a participating-government monitoring report, not an independent UN panel finding. This is part of the case that North Korea's strategic position has improved, even though it also draws the country further into a costly war.

    Evidence and earlier preparation · global-player

    Evidence and preparation

    This brings the North and South back into the same argument. Their forms of power differ, and their roles are not equivalent. But neither can be left out of an account of European security. The South's arms exports to Poland support a NATO member's capacity. The North's support helps Russia wage its war against Ukraine. Following Korea helps us understand a conflict thousands of miles away.

    Capabilities and relationships change other states’ choices

    Hwasong-17: liquid fuel · Hwasong-19: solid fuel, tested 2024 · missile testing does not establish every claimed capability
    Deterrence does not make war impossible

    Supporting explanation

    The leadership treats nuclear weapons and missiles as protection against outside attack and attempts to remove it. We do not have to endorse that policy to understand the importance it assigns those weapons. Deterrence does not make war impossible. It changes other governments’ choices.

    Russia’s war has given North Korea something to supply that a major power wants: weapons and troops. Their treaty and military cooperation give the North additional support and bargaining power. Russia has also obstructed international sanctions monitoring.

    These are reasons for endurance. The North’s position has changed. Its economy has adapted too.

    State ownership and market activity coexist

    Different products, producers and customers

    Selected official product images · availability does not establish household affordability

    Supporting explanation

    State ownership and market activity can coexist. Enterprises produce differentiated goods; shops, showrooms and licensed markets sell them. Households find ways to earn income and obtain what they need.

    Look at the products. Maebongsan and Ryuwon shoes. Unhasu and Pomhyanggi cosmetics. Foods, soap, bottled drinks, competing beer brands. Someone makes these, sells them, buys them, and judges their quality.

    Different products do not prove everyone can afford them. They do show economic activity that a picture of an empty, motionless country leaves out.

    Recovery and development, with real limits

    3.5% estimated growth · 2025

    Three years of growth · still below 2016

    Regional policy target: 20 cities/counties a year · 10 years

    Bank of Korea · July 2026 · selected official images · sustained services depend on staffing, power, supplies and access; buildings do not establish household welfare

    Supporting explanation

    South Korea’s central bank estimates that the North’s economy grew in 2023, 2024, and 2025. The 2025 estimate is 3.5 percent. Output was still below its 2016 level. Recovery is different from prosperity.

    The twenty-by-ten program aims to develop regional industries in twenty cities and counties each year for ten years. Kujang, Ryonggang, Jongphyong: factories, a hospital, a service center. Operation depends on staffing, electricity, supplies and access. Pyongyang’s new streets show construction and a particular distribution of resources; they do not stand for every North Korean life.

    Internal control, deterrence, external support, and adaptation. Together they explain more than the familiar bogeyman on the verge of collapse.

    Wisconsin also faces an aging workforce

    IFR · Korean final birth statistics · automation does not settle the pressures of work, care and family life

    Supporting explanation

    There are pressures against my forecast. South Korea is aging. Its fertility rate rose to 0.80 in 2025, still far below replacement. Wisconsin knows about an aging workforce and the need for care.

    Korean factories had 1,220 industrial robots per ten thousand manufacturing workers in 2024. Automation helps production. It does not settle family life, elder care, housing, or who shares the benefits. We face related problems. We can learn from Korea’s responses.

    Sources and supporting detail

    Workers, care, families

    Evidence and earlier preparation · robots

    Evidence and preparation

    The IFR April 2026 release gives 1220 industrial robots per 10000 manufacturing employees in Korea, 446 in Japan and 307 in the US for 2024. That is almost four times US density. Electronics and automotive manufacturing are important to Korea’s figure. This is not a count of humanoids, and low fertility by itself does not prove the cause of automation. Wisconsin has its own workforce pressures. The optional Atlas clip is training at Hyundai’s facility, a future-facing application after the evidence of automation already in use. Video source is sponsored Bloomberg Media Studios content presented by Hyundai, clearly identified.

    Evidence and earlier preparation · birth-rate

    Evidence and preparation

    South Korea’s total fertility rate rose from 0.72 in 2023 to 0.75 in 2024 and 0.80 in 2025. This is a modest rise, not a new record low. Total fertility rate summarizes a year’s age-specific birth rates: it is not the completed family size of today’s young women, not a prediction that each woman will have 0.80 children. About 2.1 is a replacement benchmark for a low-mortality population without migration; it does not predict a population’s near-term size. Wisconsin is not at the same fertility level. But our Department of Workforce Development also identifies an aging population as a challenge for worker availability. Care, work and family life connect the two stories. The preceding robot slide shows one technological capacity, not proof that low fertility caused Korea’s robot adoption.

    Koreans will make choices within that changing balance. Follow the capabilities, the constraints, and the relationships. Then judge how the forecast develops.

    Division is durable. Its future is not settled.

    An armistice, without a final peace settlement

    My forecast · next 10–15 years

    Less American predominance. More possibility for Korean unification.

    Korean choices · China’s interests · security arrangements

    A serious obstacle: Pyongyang treats the South as a hostile separate state.

    Earlier detailed predictions and Wisconsin proposal

    What is likely?My forecast · next 10–15 years

    한국 / 조선 · Korea

    Stronger Koreas

    More independence. More influence.

    United States

    Less dominance

    Wisconsin / Fox Valley

    Trade, investment, friendship.

    Possible: Neenah–Jeonju sister cities through paper

    When you follow Korea, you're ahead of the world.

    Keep learning. Keep trading. Keep building together.

    친구CHINGU

    Supporting explanation

    An armistice stopped the fighting in 1953 without a final peace settlement. The division has lasted a long time. That does not mean every part of it must last forever.

    As American predominance declines, I expect the possibility of Korean unification to increase. A more capable South Korea may seek greater freedom to arrange its own security. Changes in outside support and pressure may change what each Korean government considers possible. Arrangements that once appeared fixed could become negotiable.

    China would have a strong interest in the outcome. So would the United States. But Koreans would have to make and sustain the agreement. Neither outside power can simply supply the political trust that requires.

    There is a serious obstacle to my argument: the North’s leadership has moved toward treating the South as a hostile separate state. Both governments also have institutions and interests bound up with continued division. A change in the balance of power could reinforce division as well as loosen it.

    I expect the possibility to grow. I am not promising one Korea by a particular year. Peace and renewed contact have value before unification. Over the next ten to fifteen years, we should consider those possibilities seriously instead of waiting for the North to collapse.

    Sources and supporting detail

    1953 · An armistice

    Evidence and earlier preparation · unification

    Evidence and preparation

    The armistice stopped the fighting; it was not a final peace settlement. We should be able to imagine a different future without assuming it will arrive soon. North Korea has moved away from its old unification policy toward treating the South as a hostile separate state. That is a major obstacle to the optimistic scenario. A future opening would require political decisions, security arrangements and enormous institutional work. Even short of unification, reduced danger and greater contact would have value.

    Wisconsin can learn in both directions

    588 students from Korea at UW–Madison · 2025–26

    Translation · Lawrence · Appleton

    Buddhist · Confucian · Shamanic traditions
    Christians · people with no religious affiliation

    Supporting explanation

    Let me bring this back to Wisconsin. Franklin Hiram King studied farming in China, Korea and Japan. Farmers of Forty Centuries appeared in 1911. He went to learn.

    Dong-One Kim earned his master’s and doctorate at UW–Madison before becoming president of Korea University. Korean students continue to study at Wisconsin. Learning goes both ways.

    My work translating Korean Buddhist teachers and teaching at Lawrence in Appleton is another part of that exchange. It has brought me into a history that includes Buddhism, Confucian learning and family rites, shamanic practices, Christianity, and lives without religious affiliation. One label cannot describe that experience. Listening in Korean has given me more to learn, and more to bring home.

    Religious traditions

    Evidence and earlier preparation · faith

    Evidence and preparation

    Jikji is a Buddhist text. That takes us from printing to people and their traditions. Buddhist temples, Confucian family and ancestral rites, and shamanic ritual all belong in our account of Korea. These are not three exclusive boxes, and they are not the whole religious landscape. Christianity and people with no religious affiliation are major parts of South Korean society. Coexistence does not mean an absence of conflict or persecution. My own Wisconsin–Korea connection includes translating Korean Buddhist teachers and teaching at Lawrence University in Appleton. Religion belongs in this talk because it is part of lived Korea—and part of my relationship with it.

    Paper and printing: a shared interest

    Oldest surviving movable-metal-type book
    78 years before Gutenberg’s Bible

    Neenah’s paper heritage · Korea’s printing heritage

    Paper and printing · industrial knowledge · museums · education

    Jikji: Bibliothèque nationale de France · The Jeonju sister-city proposal is on the closing slide.

    Supporting explanation

    In a paper town, start with paper. This is Jikji, a Buddhist book printed with movable metal type in Cheongju in 1377, seventy-eight years before Gutenberg’s Bible. The oldest surviving book printed with that technology.

    The Fox Valley’s paper heritage gives us a reason to develop another relationship. The current proposal is Jeonju, a city with a living hanji tradition. Jikji belongs to Cheongju and remains here as evidence of Korea’s printing history. Industrial knowledge, museums, education, and people interested in how things are made give an exchange substance.

    Sources and supporting detail

    In a paper town, start with paper

    Evidence and earlier preparation · jikji

    Evidence and preparation

    This is Jikji, a Buddhist text printed in Cheongju. The surviving metal-type volume is in the National Library of France. It does not mean that all later European printing descended from Korea; that is a different historical claim. It means that a familiar story of technological invention is incomplete when Korea is left out. Korea's present capabilities have a history. We should not reduce the entire country to a recent miracle of catching up.

    Getting Korea Right, Getting Ourselves Right, Getting the World Right

    Evidence and earlier preparation · rogers

    Evidence and preparation

    Jim Rogers has made a bullish case for a unified Korea. This is a dated quotation from 2018, not a new forecast. He emphasized the combination of the South's capital and know-how with the North's people, resources and location. His confidence is an investor's thesis, not proof that political barriers will disappear. My use of 'long Korea' is broader: invest attention, knowledge and relationships in a place whose importance we still underestimate. Rogers is one investor with a dated formulation of that possibility. The point is to invest attention and relationships in Korea already, rather than waiting for unification.

      Evidence and earlier preparation · wisconsin-ginseng

      Evidence and preparation

      Ginseng belongs in this talk alongside chips and ships. Wisconsin grows American ginseng; Korean ginseng is a different species. The state agriculture department currently says almost 98% of US production comes from Wisconsin, with Marathon County producing about 95% of the state crop. Earlier drafts used 90–95%; this slide uses the stable phrase nearly all. Korea’s long association with ginseng creates a familiar cultural and commercial connection, not proof that Korea buys most Wisconsin production. The original tariff comparison is preserved in the original slide, explicitly a 2012 KORUS base schedule; 754% must not be presented as today’s tariff.

      Evidence and preparation

      Here is a different image to hold alongside the night photograph. New high-rise streets are real construction, even when their presentation is carefully managed by state media.       Evidence and earlier preparation · beyond-capital

      Evidence and preparation

      38 North documented the first two rounds of the regional development program. This map shows selected cities and counties, not exact factory coordinates. The program is expanding the visible investment beyond central Pyongyang. The next issue is whether these facilities receive reliable power, materials and workers and deliver useful output. Building openings are evidence of construction; they are not a substitute for production data.

      Evidence and earlier preparation · consumer-life

      Evidence and preparation

      Wisconsin is a good place to recognize a brewery and a beer brand. These dated official photographs show products, branding and a venue intended for customers. They complicate an image of a country with no commercial life. They do not give us sales volumes or tell us who can afford the products. Public and state-linked ownership can coexist with branding and retail exchange. Keep the claim about what the evidence actually shows, then let the audience see the images.

      Additional material

      A changing leadership picture

      A succession signal, not a settled outcome

      Sources and supporting detail
      Evidence and earlier preparation · kim-ju-ae

      Evidence and preparation

      These two photographs show a change we can actually observe. Kim's daughter, widely identified as Kim Ju Ae, first appeared publicly at a missile event in November 2022. In September 2025 she accompanied him to Beijing. South Korean intelligence has interpreted her prominence as preparation for succession. That is an assessment. A formal transfer of leadership has not taken place, and appearances alone cannot establish the full succession plan. We should watch the changing public presentation of the next generation without pretending we know the private decision.

      Sources and media

      • BBC: first public appearance, November 2022
      • Chosun via Nate: Beijing photograph, September 2, 2025

      Evidence and earlier preparation · missiles

      Evidence and preparation

      This photograph shows the older Hwasong-17, not the Hwasong-19. The move toward solid-fueled intercontinental missiles matters because it can reduce preparation time and complicate detection. Analysts distinguish what a launch demonstrates from claims about warheads, accuracy and reentry under operational conditions. We can recognize a serious technical advance without repeating every state claim or claiming a weapon makes war impossible.

      Sources and media

      • 38 North: analysis of October 31, 2024 Hwasong-19 test
      • Original deterrence argument — claims require qualified wording
      Evidence and earlier preparation · oshkosh-hanwha

      Evidence and preparation

      This is a local example of international technical collaboration. Oshkosh’s 2021 consortium included Hanwha Defense USA and proposed a vehicle using Hanwha’s Redback chassis. It was a concept-design award, not a production contract. The Army selected General Dynamics and American Rheinmetall for detailed design and prototype phases in June 2023. Keep both dates: the partnership is real without pretending it won the later competition.

      Sources and supporting material

      • Oshkosh Defense · July 26, 2021; U.S. Army · June 26, 2023
      • Army’s subsequent awards

      One argument

      Both Koreas have capabilities that affect decisions far beyond the peninsula. Wisconsin already has a direct engineering connection to this defense industry.

      Exact scope

      • North Korea: SIPRI estimates about60 assembled warheads in January2026; this is uncertain, not a verified count or a count of deployed warheads. The photograph shows a2022 Hwasong-17 missile display, not60 warheads or the newer Hwasong-19.
      • KF-21: Korean-led development, with international partners and components;4.5-generation, not an indigenous fifth-generation operational fighter. Photograph is prototype 006, despite its Commons filename. South Korea’s fifth-generation F-35A is U.S.-built.
      • Lowy: military-capability sub-index of the2025 Asia Power Index, not a global overall-power ranking or a combat prediction. Ranks1–7 shown. Scores:88.9,70.6,55.4,48.0,33.2,31.1,30.1. The nuclear estimate is separate evidence; do not describe this rank as a nuclear-warhead ranking.
      • Global export rank: SIPRI2021–25 major-arms transfer volume; South Korea9th,3.0% global share. Not dollar sales or announced contracts.
      • Oshkosh–Hanwha:2021 OMFV concept-design collaboration using Hanwha’s Redback chassis. The Army selected other teams in2023. This does not establish joint production in Korea; Hanwha’s announcement envisaged U.S. production.

      Evidence and earlier preparation · culture

      Evidence and preparation

      Some of us first met Korea through the war or through M*A*S*H. A younger generation encounters Korean music, Korean storytelling and Korean settings without needing an introduction. These examples are different kinds of production: KPop Demon Hunters is a Sony Pictures Animation film released by Netflix, shaped by Korean culture and international collaboration. The point is global influence, not that every production here was made by a Korean company. Play a short section of Golden, then continue. Use the button for a twenty-second excerpt, 0:45–1:05; leaving this slide stops the player. This turns recognition into a brief shared experience. Streaming needs internet.

      Evidence and earlier preparation · robots

      Evidence and preparation

      The IFR April 2026 release gives 1220 industrial robots per 10000 manufacturing employees in Korea, 446 in Japan and 307 in the US for 2024. That is almost four times US density. Electronics and automotive manufacturing are important to Korea’s figure. This is not a count of humanoids, and low fertility by itself does not prove the cause of automation. Wisconsin has its own workforce pressures. The optional Atlas clip is training at Hyundai’s facility, a future-facing application after the evidence of automation already in use. Video source is sponsored Bloomberg Media Studios content presented by Hyundai, clearly identified.

      Sources and media

      • IFR · April 2026 release; 2024 data
      • Wisconsin DWD · workforce profiles
      • Bloomberg Media Studios / Hyundai · Inside the Robotics Race
      • Demographic change — original source needs a current primary-source check
      Evidence and earlier preparation · birth-rate

      Evidence and preparation

      South Korea’s total fertility rate rose from 0.72 in 2023 to 0.75 in 2024 and 0.80 in 2025. This is a modest rise, not a new record low. Total fertility rate summarizes a year’s age-specific birth rates: it is not the completed family size of today’s young women, not a prediction that each woman will have 0.80 children. About 2.1 is a replacement benchmark for a low-mortality population without migration; it does not predict a population’s near-term size. Wisconsin is not at the same fertility level. But our Department of Workforce Development also identifies an aging population as a challenge for worker availability. Care, work and family life connect the two stories. The preceding robot slide shows one technological capacity, not proof that low fertility caused Korea’s robot adoption.

      Evidence and earlier preparation · memory

      Evidence and preparation

      DRAM is working memory used by computers. The chart measures revenue across the whole DRAM market in Q 2 2026. Samsung 39.4 plus SKhynix 24.9 equals 64.3 percent. That is not a count of chips and not a measure of where factories sit. Now connect the broader industry to AI: high-bandwidth memory is specialized DRAM that supplies data rapidly to AI processors. The function diagram makes that separate connection; the chart is not an HBM market-share chart.

      Sources and media

      • TrendForce · Q2 2026 DRAM revenue
      • SK hynix · HBM4 for AI
      Evidence and earlier preparation · ships

      Evidence and preparation

      This is completed commercial shipbuilding output, measured in gross tonnage, a measure of enclosed volume. It is not vessel count, new orders or naval shipbuilding. Korea accounts for 28.02 percent; the United States 0.04 percent. The tiny American bar is drawn to the same scale and may be barely visible. The numbers explain why Korean expertise and investment matter in Philadelphia. Hanwha’s five-billion-dollar announcement is a plan, not completed spending. The American relationship is about capabilities in both directions.

      Latitude comparison

      Madison 43.1°N · Seoul 37.6°N · San Francisco 37.8°N

      Korea shifted only in longitude for this comparison · latitude is not climate

      Supporting explanation

      Seoul is south of Madison, almost at San Francisco's latitude.

      Sources and supporting detail
      Evidence and earlier preparation · where

      Evidence and preparation

      Put the peninsula back into the audience’s mental map. China and Russia meet North Korea; Japan lies across the sea. Seoul and Pyongyang are close enough to share a regional future, but their governments are separated by a militarized border. Geography helps explain repeated outside involvement without making Koreans passive objects of it. Original Natural Earth geometry and capital locators retained; this is a regional orientation map, not a travel map.

      Evidence and earlier preparation · latitude

      Evidence and preparation

      The familiar cold-war imagery can obscure the geography. Seoul is about five and a half degrees south of Madison. City values use weather-station coordinates rounded to one decimal, not city boundaries. Korea’s mountains, continental air masses and surrounding seas also affect its weather.

      Evidence and earlier preparation · opening

      Evidence and preparation

      Thank you for having me. This is a talk about Korea, but it is also a talk about us: our history, our work, our children and grandchildren. We tend to recognize the importance of China and Japan. Korea deserves that same serious attention—both Koreas. The claim tonight is that understanding Korea helps us see our own country and the world more clearly.
